feedback.worked_solution:
Previously, we found that

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=-10x{y}^{2}-4x,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=-4{y}^{3}-10{x}^{2}y+20y.
$$

Computing the second partial derivatives, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-10x{y}^{2}-4x)=-10{y}^{2}-4 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x}=\frac{∂}{∂x}(-10x{y}^{2}-4x)=-20xy \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-4{y}^{3}-10{x}^{2}y+20y)=-12{y}^{2}-10{x}^{2}+20\end{aligned}
$$
